title: Confession rhythm
hook: some Catholics go monthly, others by season
tomorrow: can you live on one gospel passage a day?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: the center. Sunday holds the week together, Mass first, then rest. Today, a rhythm on a longer clock.

The dentist sends the reminder text. The car flashes its oil light. The phone wants an update, again. Everything you care about comes with a maintenance schedule. Then something happens: you snap at someone you love, and it sits in your chest for days, even after you've both said sorry. The Church has a minimum for that. And then it has a rhythm.
screen: `EVERYTHING HAS A SCHEDULE.` → `IT SITS IN YOUR CHEST.` → `A MINIMUM, THEN A RHYTHM.`

segments.voice: The minimum is in Church law: confess serious sins at least once a year. That's a floor, not a goal. The Church also encourages confessing everyday faults, because grace is there for those too, and because small habits are where big ones start. So Catholics build rhythms. Some go monthly. Some go in Advent and Lent, when parishes may hold penance services. Some tie it to a date they won't forget. Why a rhythm, and not just when it gets bad? Because a return gets easier the more you make it. The son in Luke's parable rehearses a whole speech on the road home. He barely gets to say it. In the Douay-Rheims: "And when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and running to him fell upon his neck, and kissed him." The father ran. Then he calls for the best robe, a ring and a feast. Coming home isn't a hearing; it's a party. And John's letter promises the outcome every time: "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just, to forgive us our sins." A rhythm just means you don't wait for a crisis to come home.
screen: `ONCE A YEAR: A FLOOR.` · `EVERYDAY FAULTS TOO.` · `THE FATHER RAN.` · `NO NEED TO WAIT FOR A CRISIS.` · then, large: `A REGULAR RETURN.`

segments.voice: Open your calendar, or take a pen. Choose your rhythm, monthly or by season, and write the next date down. Then sit quietly with one thing you'd bring. No speech rehearsed, the way the son never got to finish his.
Confession rhythm. A regular return to the sacrament, chosen ahead of time, not saved for a crisis.
Your line: a regular return. The father in the story runs every single time. See you tomorrow.
